sentences.zh: 周日，在经历了一场许多人担心会将其彻底摧毁的大火以及一项打破所有人预期的迅速翻新之后，巴黎圣母院重新对公众开放。

sentences.en: Today, Chief Architecture Critic Michael Kimmelman with the story of the miracle on the Seine.
sentences.zh: 今天，首席建筑评论员迈克尔·金默曼将为我们讲述塞纳河畔的奇迹。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月11日，星期三。

sentences.en: Michael, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: I'm just going to acknowledge that we have been trying to get you on the show for seven years.
sentences.zh: 我只想说，我们其实已经邀请你来做节目七年了。

sentences.en: And then two days more, because over the past couple of days, there's been a tremendous amount of very serious news.
sentences.zh: 而且还要再加上两天，因为在过去的几天里，发生了大量非常重大的新闻。

sentences.en: The government in Syria fell a closely watched manhunt for the suspected murderer of the CEO of a major health care company.
sentences.zh: 叙利亚政权倒台，以及对一名大型医疗公司首席执行官疑似谋杀案的密切搜捕。

sentences.en: that case got cracked wide open, all of which delayed this much-awaited debut of yours on the show.
sentences.zh: 这个案件取得了重大突破，所有这些都耽误了你这场备受期待的节目首秀。

sentences.en: And today is the day.
sentences.zh: 而今天就是这一天。

sentences.en: You, our chief architecture critic, finally here talking about something worthy of your biography, Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 你，我们的首席建筑评论员，终于来到这里谈论一件配得上你履历的事物——巴黎圣母院。

sentences.en: So welcome.
sentences.zh: 所以，欢迎。

sentences.en: Well, better late than never, I hope.
sentences.zh: 嗯，希望迟到总比不到好。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, just to begin, do you remember the first time you stepped inside that?
sentences.zh: 那么，首先，你还记得你第一次走进去是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: cathedral i mean i remember as a boy going with my family and we had come from the soviet union
sentences.zh: 我是指那座大教堂，我记得还是个男孩的时候和家人一起去，我们当时从苏联来

sentences.en: where i was unable to find milk i was probably eight paris it turns out has milk it was cold
sentences.zh: 在那里我买不到牛奶，我大概八岁，原来巴黎有牛奶，当时很冷

sentences.en: but i do remember going into the cathedral and feeling somehow warmed when i went in there
sentences.zh: 但我确实记得走进大教堂，进去时不知怎的感到心里暖洋洋的

sentences.en: So that was my first impression.
sentences.zh: 所以那是我的第一印象。

sentences.en: I guess it stuck with me in some way.
sentences.zh: 我想它在某种程度上留在了我的记忆里。

sentences.en: So your memory of it is vague, but the impression I'm getting is that whatever it did to you, it did something.
sentences.zh: 所以你的记忆很模糊，但给我的感觉是，无论它对你做了什么，它确实产生了某种影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it does to millions and millions of people who have no religious connection to it.
sentences.zh: 对，我想它对千百万与它没有宗教联系的人也是如此。

sentences.en: It was a place that people imagined they had to go to if they went to Paris.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们去巴黎时觉得必须去的地方。

sentences.en: You didn't see Paris unless you went to Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 如果你没去巴黎圣母院，就不算看过巴黎。

sentences.en: So let's fast forward a good deal to several years ago.
sentences.zh: 那我们快进很多，来到好几年前。

sentences.en: Where were you when you first heard that Notre Dame was burning?
sentences.zh: 你第一次听说巴黎圣母院着火时在哪里？

sentences.en: I remember very vividly where I was.
sentences.zh: 我非常清晰地记得我在哪里。

sentences.en: I was on my bike, rushing to an appointment on the west side of Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我当时正骑着自行车，急着赶去曼哈顿西区的一个约会。

sentences.en: My phone rang, and it was an editor here at The Times who sounded a little frantic.
sentences.zh: 我的电话响了，是《时报》的一位编辑，听起来有点惊慌。

sentences.en: And told me I had to rush back and write something because Notre Dame was burning.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我必须赶紧回去写点东西，因为巴黎圣母院着火了。

sentences.en: And I thought he was crazy.
sentences.zh: 而我觉得他疯了。

sentences.en: Crazy, why?
sentences.zh: 疯了，为什么？

sentences.en: Because Notre Dame has a giant stone building.
sentences.zh: 因为巴黎圣母院是一座巨大的石头建筑。

sentences.en: I didn't think it could burn down.
sentences.zh: 我以为它不可能烧毁。

sentences.en: And it sounded sort of inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 听起来简直不可思议。

sentences.en: It's like EvereSt.
sentences.zh: 就像珠穆朗玛峰一样。

sentences.en: It doesn't burn down.
sentences.zh: 它不会被烧毁。

sentences.en: The pyramids do not burn down.
sentences.zh: 金字塔也不会被烧毁。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: And I said, I'm sorry to tell you this, but his name is also Michael.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，很抱歉告诉你这个，但他名字也叫迈克尔。

sentences.en: So I said, Michael, that doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，迈克尔，这说不通。

sentences.en: He said, I think you just better look on your phone.
sentences.zh: 他说，我想你最好还是看一眼手机。

sentences.en: And I went to find a live feed, and there it was.
sentences.zh: 于是我去找直播画面，然后它就出现在那里。

sentences.en: I'm now turning to the back of the cathedral.
sentences.zh: 我现在转向大教堂的背面。

sentences.en: It is a terrible scene here.
sentences.zh: 这里是一个可怕的场景。

sentences.en: The roof has entirely collapsed.
sentences.zh: 屋顶已经完全坍塌了。

sentences.en: There are flames coming out of the back of the cathedral as if it was a torch.
sentences.zh: 大教堂的背面冒出熊熊烈火，就像一个火炬。

sentences.en: It looks like the Olympic torch from the back.
sentences.zh: 从背面看就像奥运火炬。

sentences.en: I remember standing there on the corner, just frozen, staring at this sight, which seemed inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己站在那个街角，简直呆住了，凝视着这看似不可思议的景象。

sentences.en: And then Twitter was just full of Pray for Paris hashtag, and everybody was suddenly fixated.
sentences.zh: 然后推特上到处都是“为巴黎祈祷”的标签，每个人突然都目不转睛地盯着。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the sign from God.
sentences.zh: 也许这是上帝的迹象。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It's not normal.
sentences.zh: 这太不正常了。

sentences.en: It really was as if the world had stopped.
sentences.zh: 真的就像世界停止了转动。

sentences.en: I see people crying, I see a lot of emotions, and I'm shocked myself.
sentences.zh: 我看到人们在哭泣，我看到了许多情绪，我自己也很震惊。

sentences.en: It's like your family loses somebody.
sentences.zh: 就像你的家人失去了某个人。

sentences.en: Both my sister and I said, you know, we are actually feeling physical pain watching Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 我和我姐姐都说，你知道，看着巴黎圣母院燃烧，我们真的感到了身体上的痛楚。

sentences.en: You feel like it's part of you.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得它是你的一部分。

sentences.en: And when you look at this 12th century medieval cathedral up in flames, it's like a knife.
sentences.zh: 当你看到这座12世纪的中世纪大教堂在大火中熊熊燃烧时，就像挨了一刀。

sentences.en: It's very hard for me not to cry right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在很难忍住不哭。

sentences.en: And I've been crying on and off the whole day.
sentences.zh: 我一整天都在断断续续地哭。

sentences.en: It just has touched me and touched everyone in France, I think, very, very deeply.
sentences.zh: 这件事真的深深地触动了我，我想也触动了法国的每一个人。

sentences.en: It occurred to me at that moment, too, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我也突然觉得，这很有意思。

sentences.en: I mean, why had the world stopped?
sentences.zh: 我是说，为什么世界会停转？

sentences.en: Why did this building mean so much to so many different people?
sentences.zh: 为什么这座建筑对这么多不同的人有如此重大的意义？

sentences.en: Not just people in France, but obviously all around the world.
sentences.zh: 不仅是对法国人，显然对全世界都是如此。

sentences.en: So I rushed back to my computer.
sentences.zh: 于是我冲回电脑前。

sentences.en: I started making a few phone calls and trying to figure that out, trying to understand what the building had meant over time.
sentences.zh: 我开始打几个电话，试图弄清楚这一点，试图理解这座建筑随着时间的推移意味着什么。

sentences.en: And to see really what the building now represented to people, what this potential disaster, I mean, it was certainly a disaster, but there was the fear, of course,
sentences.zh: 并真正看看这座建筑现在对人们代表着什么，这场潜在的灾难——我的意思是，这当然是一场灾难，但当然也有一种恐惧

sentences.en: that the building would disappear.
sentences.zh: 那就是这座建筑会消失。

sentences.en: That this would be the moment after almost 900 years that we were living at that moment when this building would go away.
sentences.zh: 在经历了将近900年之后，我们将经历这样一个时刻：这座建筑将不复存在。

sentences.en: Well, I'm curious,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很好奇，

sentences.en: when this inquiry is moving along and you're making phone calls and you're researching the history of Notre Dame and trying to understand why the feelings about its burning are so widespread and so deep,
sentences.zh: 当这种调查不断推进，你打着电话，研究巴黎圣母院的历史，并试图理解为什么人们对它燃烧的感受如此广泛且深厚时，

sentences.en: what do you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think, Michael, you have to step back and say, what is the meaning of a building?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，迈克尔，你必须退一步想想，一座建筑的意义究竟是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, for me, architecture is really the world we built and are building.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我来说，建筑实际上就是我们建造以及正在建造的世界。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people have talked about it as a kind of aesthetic thing, and that is one aspect of it for sure.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人把它谈论成一种审美的东西，这当然是它的一个方面。

sentences.en: And I think the conversation around architecture for a while sort of saw it as a branch of sculpture.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有一段时间围绕建筑的讨论似乎把它看作雕塑的一个分支。

sentences.en: You know, whether buildings were cool looking.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是建筑看起来是不是很酷。

sentences.en: They were fetishized, aestheticized.
sentences.zh: 它们被神圣化、审美化了。

sentences.en: And there's definitely an aspect of that that's important in architecture.
sentences.zh: 建筑中确实有这方面很重要的一面。

sentences.en: But I've always felt that really architecture is much larger than that.
sentences.zh: 但我一直觉得建筑实际上远比这宏大。

sentences.en: Buildings are living things that exist in our lives, in our neighborhoods, communities, cities.
sentences.zh: 建筑是活生生的事物，存在于我们的生活、我们的街区、社区和城市中。

sentences.en: And they're there whether we choose to look at them or not.
sentences.zh: 无论我们选择不选择看它们，它们都在那里。

sentences.en: They have to be used.
sentences.zh: 它们必须被使用。

sentences.en: And so really they raise these questions of what do they say about us as a society?
sentences.zh: 所以它们确实提出了这样的问题：它们对我们这个社会意味着什么？

sentences.en: And in the case of Notre Dame, it's been speaking.
sentences.zh: 而在巴黎圣母院的例子中，它一直在诉说。

sentences.en: It's meant things to people over generations, over centuries, for almost a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 世世代代、几个世纪以来，近千年来，它对人们都有着特殊的意义。

sentences.en: Well, tell us a little bit about that history.
sentences.zh: 好吧，给我们讲讲这段历史吧。

sentences.en: And I suspect through that, we will understand what it has meant to us during that entire period.
sentences.zh: 我猜通过这些，我们会理解它在整个时期对我们的意义。

sentences.en: Well, I think, you know, the building has had a lot of meanings over time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，你知道，随着时间的推移，这座建筑有很多含义。

sentences.en: You, first of all, have to see where it sits geographically.
sentences.zh: 首先，你必须看看它的地理位置。

sentences.en: It sits at the center of Paris on an island.
sentences.zh: 它位于巴黎市中心的一个岛上。

sentences.en: in the middle of the Seine River.
sentences.zh: 在塞纳河的正中央。

sentences.en: And that island is where what came to be called Paris started.
sentences.zh: 那个岛正是后来被称为巴黎的发源地。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: It had been a prehistoric settlement and then was an ancient settlement.
sentences.zh: 它曾是一个史前定居点，后来又是一个古代定居点。

sentences.en: The Romans settled there.
sentences.zh: 罗马人曾在此定居。

sentences.en: It was a Gallo-Roman town called Lutetia, occupied by the Parisi.
sentences.zh: 这是一个名叫卢泰西亚的高卢-罗马城镇，由巴黎西人居住。

sentences.en: I didn't know any of this.
sentences.zh: 这些我一点都不知道。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不用谢。

sentences.en: I hope it's true.
sentences.zh: 希望这是真的。

sentences.en: And then when the church was there, there was original religious buildings and sanctuaries built on the island over centuries.
sentences.zh: 后来当教会进驻时，几个世纪以来，岛上建立起了最初的宗教建筑和圣殿。

sentences.en: It was invaded by Vikings.
sentences.zh: 它遭到过维京人的入侵。

sentences.en: And then eventually in the 12th century, a bishop of Paris decided that they should build a Gothic cathedral there.
sentences.zh: 最终在12世纪，巴黎的一位主教决定在那里建造一座哥特式大教堂。

sentences.en: And this was the new style.
sentences.zh: 这就是全新的风格。

sentences.en: It was little like the pyramids in the sense that these were buildings of an incredible scale and ambition and weirdness.
sentences.zh: 它有点像金字塔，因为这些建筑规模宏大、雄心勃勃且独具匠心。

sentences.en: majesty, complexity.
sentences.zh: 雄伟、复杂。

sentences.en: So they tore down some of the old church buildings, which were on the east end of the island, and started erecting this building.
sentences.zh: 于是他们拆毁了岛东端的一些旧教堂建筑，开始兴建这座建筑。

sentences.en: And since then, that was in the 1160s, the building has remained the center of the city.
sentences.zh: 从那时起——那是1160年代，这座建筑一直是城市的中心。

sentences.en: It's essentially witnessed the growth of the city.
sentences.zh: 它基本上见证了这座城市的成长。

sentences.en: It's been the sun around which the city has revolved.
sentences.zh: 它是城市环绕旋转的太阳。

sentences.en: It's the place from which all distances in France are measured, literally.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上，法国所有的距离都是从这个地方开始测量的。

sentences.en: There's a plaque on the plaza in front of it.
sentences.zh: 它正前方的广场上有一块牌匾。

sentences.en: In other words, all French roads quite literally lead to this cathedral.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，字面意思上，法国所有的道路都通向这座大教堂。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In a sense, everything circulates around it.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，一切都围绕着它运转。

sentences.en: But I think also it has witnessed a lot of important events in French history.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它也见证了法国历史上许多重要的事件。

sentences.en: Mary, Queen of Scots, was married there.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽曾在此举行婚礼。

sentences.en: Napoleon was coronated there.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑曾在此加冕。

sentences.en: And when the revolution happened, you had, you know, the insurgence of the revolution.
sentences.zh: 当大革命爆发时，你知道，革命的起义者们来了。

sentences.en: They ransacked Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 他们洗劫了巴黎圣母院。

sentences.en: It was a symbol.
sentences.zh: 它是一个象征。

sentences.en: They hated the church.
sentences.zh: 他们痛恨教会。

sentences.en: They knocked off the heads of the Old Testament figures on the front who they thought were kings.
sentences.zh: 他们砸掉了正面旧约人物的头像，因为他们认为那些是国王。

sentences.en: And they melted down the bells and turned them into cannonballs and coins.
sentences.zh: 他们把大钟融化，铸成炮弹和硬币。

sentences.en: It's fascinating because what could better embody the idea of a single building's importance to a place than it becomes a central target of an effort to overturn the entire system?
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为有什么能比一座单独的建筑成为推翻整个体系努力的核心目标，更能体现它对一个地方的重要性呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: By the time of Napoleon, right after the revolution, the place was a wreck.
sentences.zh: 到了拿破仑时期，大革命刚结束时，这个地方成了一片废墟。

sentences.en: It was a dump.
sentences.zh: 简直是个垃圾场。

sentences.en: It had been ruined during the revolution, but it was also falling apart.
sentences.zh: 它在大革命期间遭到破坏，而且也正在分崩离析。

sentences.en: When Napoleon decided to have his coronation there, it was so bad that he had to get a couple of architects, like very high-level interior decorators,
sentences.zh: 当拿破仑决定在那里加冕时，情况糟透了，他不得不找来几位建筑师，就像顶级室内装饰师那样，

sentences.en: to basically hang a lot of tapestries to cover up all the mess behind it, like a stage set.
sentences.zh: 基本上挂上了许多挂毯，把后面所有的杂乱都遮掩起来，就像一个舞台布景。

sentences.en: And then that also caused Victor Hugo, the writer, to write a book about a hunchback bell ringer.
sentences.zh: 这也促使作家维克多·雨果写了一本关于驼背敲钟人的书。

sentences.en: I've heard of it.
sentences.zh: 我听说过。

sentences.en: He spends a chapter lamenting what had happened to Notre Dame, that this was said, what it said about France and what Notre Dame meant to the country.
sentences.zh: 他花了一个章节来哀叹巴黎圣母院所遭遇的不幸，这一切是多么令人痛心，它对法国意味着什么，以及巴黎圣母院对这个国家的意义。

sentences.en: I don't think we can miss an opportunity, since you brought it with you, to read from The Hunchback of Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 既然你把书带来了，我觉得我们不能错过这个机会，读一读《巴黎圣母院》里的片段。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He wrote in, shall we say, ripe prose and in long, voluptuous sentences.
sentences.zh: 他的文风可以说是成熟老练，句子冗长而缠绵。

sentences.en: But I'll read you a couple.
sentences.zh: 不过我读几句给你听。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: So, first of all, he begins this chapter about Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 那么，首先，他以这段话开启了关于巴黎圣母院的章节。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: The Church of Notre Dame de Paris is without doubt, even today, a sublime and majestic building.
sentences.zh: 巴黎圣母院毫无疑问，即使在今天，也是一座宏伟壮丽的建筑。

sentences.en: But however much it may have conserved its beauty as it has grown older, it is hard not to regret,
sentences.zh: 但无论它在日渐苍老的过程中如何保持着它的美丽，人们很难不感到惋惜，

sentences.en: not to feel indignation at the numberless degradations and mutilations which time and men have wrought simultaneously on this venerable monument.
sentences.zh: 很难不对时间和人类同时对这座古老纪念碑造成的无数破坏和摧残感到愤怒。

sentences.en: It's a cold arMs.
sentences.zh: 这是一个冷酷的武器。

sentences.en: It's a call to arms, exactly.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是战斗的号角。

sentences.en: Great buildings, he says, like great mountains, are the works of centuries.
sentences.zh: 他说，伟大的建筑就像伟大的山脉一样，是数个世纪的结晶。

sentences.en: The man, the individual, and the artist are erased from these great piles, which bear no author's name.
sentences.zh: 人类、个人和艺术家在这些没有作者署名的庞大建筑中都被抹去了。

sentences.en: They are the summary and summation of human intelligence.
sentences.zh: 它们是人类智慧的总结与总和。

sentences.en: Time is the architect, the nation, the builder.
sentences.zh: 时间是建筑师，民族是建造者。

sentences.en: Which I think is interesting, Michael, because that's the point.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我觉得这很有意思，因为这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: Notre Dame, for him, represented France.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，巴黎圣母院代表了法国。

sentences.en: And so its recovery, its preservation, was about France's preservation, its heritage, its strength.
sentences.zh: 因此，它的修复、它的保护，关乎法国的保护、它的遗产和它的力量。

sentences.en: Hugo had no particular patience with the church, but he believed that the building itself meant a lot to the nation.
sentences.zh: 雨果对教会并没有什么耐心，但他相信这座建筑本身对国家意义重大。

sentences.en: And that book came at the same time as a movement was rising in France to preserve its heritage.
sentences.zh: 那本书出版的同时，法国正兴起一股保护其遗产的运动。

sentences.en: And those two things led to the restoration of Notre Dame in the 19th century to prevent its collapse, basically, and to restore it.
sentences.zh: 这两件事促成了19世纪巴黎圣母院的修复，主要是为了防止其倒塌并将其修缮完好。

sentences.en: And that was a key moment in the history of not just Notre Dame and Paris, but the whole idea of historic preservation globally.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是巴黎圣母院和巴黎历史上的一个关键时刻，也是全球历史保护理念的关键时刻。

sentences.en: It reminds me of what you said at the beginning of this conversation about architecture, is that this is not some abstract piece of architecture.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起你在这次对话开头关于建筑所说的话，即这不是某种抽象的建筑片段。

sentences.en: It's living, it's breathing, it tells us something essential about who we are at any given moment.
sentences.zh: 它是活生生的，它在呼吸，它向我们诉说着在任何特定时刻我们究竟是谁这一本质。

sentences.en: And Hugo, as you said, he's not saying that through an especially religious lens.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，雨果并不是通过特别宗教的视角来看待这一切的。

sentences.en: He's seeing this more as a secular temple.
sentences.zh: 他更多地将其视为一座世俗的圣殿。

sentences.en: A palace of the people.
sentences.zh: 人民的宫殿。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He saw it as representing all sorts of romantic ideals about the people, about community, about glory.
sentences.zh: 他认为它代表了关于人民、关于社区、关于荣耀的各种浪漫理想。

sentences.en: And that book helped inspire the renovation of the cathedral in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 那本书帮助激发了19世纪大教堂的翻修。

sentences.en: It was brought back.
sentences.zh: 它重获新生了。

sentences.en: We got the spire that then became famous on the Paris skyline.
sentences.zh: 我们有了后来成为巴黎天际线标志的尖顶。

sentences.en: Hugo's book also made it more of an attraction.
sentences.zh: 雨果的书也让它成为了一个更具吸引力的景点。

sentences.en: People wanted to come to Paris to see the building.
sentences.zh: 人们想要来巴黎看这座建筑。

sentences.en: Eventually, Disney wanted to make movies about it.
sentences.zh: 最终，迪士尼想要以它为题材制作电影。

sentences.en: People from all over the world came.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们纷至沓来。

sentences.en: More of them then went to see the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
sentences.zh: 随后，去巴黎看埃菲尔铁塔的人反而变多了。

sentences.en: More of them then went to visit the St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
sentences.zh: 后来去罗马参观圣彼得大教堂的人也变多了。

sentences.en: And in that sense, it really did become truly a palace of the people.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，它真的成为了名副其实的人民宫殿。

sentences.en: And so what did this fire say about us, about this moment, that the horror of it was that our moment would be the moment
sentences.zh: 那么，这场大火对我们、对这个时代意味着什么？最可怕的是，我们的时代竟然会成为

sentences.en: when this building across this great arc of history would disappear?
sentences.zh: 这座历经历史长河的建筑消失的时刻？

sentences.en: What did that say about how we had cared for it?
sentences.zh: 这说明了我们是如何照顾它的？

sentences.en: And even the fact that it was on fire was clearly an indication that we'd been derelict.
sentences.zh: 甚至它着火这一事实，也清楚地表明我们一直玩忽职守。

sentences.en: It was a fire that never needed to happen.
sentences.zh: 这是一场本不该发生的大火。

sentences.en: It was a guy who probably left a cigarette butt, lighted in the rafters, and then somebody else who went to the wrong place to check out why there was an alarm.

sentences.zh: 它似乎反映了我们这个时代的某些问题。

sentences.zh: 既然你刚提起，提醒我们一下这场火灾究竟有多严重。

sentences.en: It was really severe.

sentences.en: And it wasn't just the roof was on fire and the spire was collapsing.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是屋顶着火、尖顶倒塌。

sentences.en: It was a very dangerous and complex thing for the firemen to try to put this fire out.

sentences.zh: 因此，由一个烟头引发的火灾，对巴黎圣母院和世界来说，实际上是一种生存危机。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 紧接着出现的问题是，在世界上如此伟大、重要、核心且受人喜爱的建筑遭到如此严重的损坏之后，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: So there were different answers to that question.
sentences.zh: 所以对于这个问题有不同的答案。

sentences.en: And at first, it wasn't clear what would happen.
sentences.zh: 起初，事情会如何发展并不明朗。

sentences.en: There were a lot of proposals to do something really crazy on the roof, to use essentially this calamity as an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 有很多提议要在屋顶上做一些非常疯狂的事情，基本上是把这场灾难当成一个机会。

sentences.zh: 怎么个疯狂法？

sentences.zh: 这简直是对你能想象到的所有奇思妙想的公开邀请。

sentences.en: Architects salivated the prospect of such a proposal.
sentences.zh: 建筑师们对这种提议垂涎三尺。

sentences.en: So circulating online pretty quickly were all sorts of things, swimming pool, garden.
sentences.zh: 所以各种各样的方案很快在网上流传开来，游泳池、花园。

sentences.en: Someone came up with the idea of like a giant carbon fiber gold leaf flame to replace the spire.
sentences.zh: 有人提出用一个巨大的碳纤维金箔火焰来取代尖顶的主意。

sentences.en: Well, that's on the nose.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可真是切中要害。

sentences.en: Yeah, it actually bore uncanny resemblance to the logo for Chicken Wings franchise in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 对，它实际上和科罗拉多州一个鸡翅连锁店的标志惊人地相似。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of those things.
sentences.zh: 这类方案有很多。

sentences.en: But relatively soon, cooler heads, including some prominent French architects, persuaded the French government to do the right thing,
sentences.zh: 但相对较快地，包括一些杰出法国建筑师在内的冷静头脑劝说法国政府做正确的事，

sentences.en: which was to restore the cathedral as it had been.
sentences.zh: 那就是将大教堂恢复原貌。

sentences.en: And that became the mission.
sentences.zh: 这就成了他们的使命。

sentences.en: And Macron, the president, even while the building was still smoldering, promised that it would be restored in five years, which back then seemed not just a Hail Mary, it seemed
sentences.zh: 总统马克龙甚至在大楼还在冒烟的时候就承诺，将在五年内将其修复，这在当时看来不仅是一个奇迹，简直是

sentences.en: It's on time, on budget, and it's incredible.

sentences.zh: 他们是如何创造这个按时完成的奇迹的？

sentences.zh: 嗯，总统马克龙指派了一位将军来负责这项行动，他叫乔治·拉讷，他像管理军事行动一样管理这件事。

sentences.zh: 它们赋予了我们彼此相连的感觉。

sentences.en: The coming together itself, which is what the cathedral is about, is a sign of hope for us.
sentences.zh: 这种聚会本身——这也是大教堂的意义所在——对我们来说是一个希望的象征。

sentences.en: It's the thing that we wish we can do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们渴望做到的事情。

sentences.en: It's our best selves.
sentences.zh: 这是我们最好的自己。

sentences.en: It's our best selves.
sentences.zh: 这是我们最好的自己。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Notre Dame is our best selves.
sentences.zh: 巴黎圣母院就是我们最好的自己。

sentences.en: And now it's in the best shape that it's ever been in probably a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 而现在，它处于可能近一千年来最好的状态。

sentences.en: If that's not a sign of human progress.
sentences.zh: 如果这还不是人类进步的象征的话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I met a lot of people, Parisians, some friends of mine, who had never really thought much about Notre Dame or actually just found an impediment on their way to work,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我遇到了很多人，巴黎人，还有我的一些朋友，他们以前从未真正多想过巴黎圣母院，或者只是觉得它是他们上班路上的阻碍，

sentences.en: all the crowds.
sentences.zh: 那些拥挤的人群。

sentences.en: And they found themselves crestfall, shocked really by how they felt when it burned.
sentences.zh: 而当它被烧毁时，他们发现自己感到沮丧，对自己的感受感到震惊。

sentences.en: And I think that was the realization for many people, that this building had a place in their own lives that they hadn't even understood before.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是许多人意识到的地方，这座建筑在他们的生活中占据着一个他们以前甚至不曾理解的位置。

sentences.en: It's a touchstone for our sense of our own changing, evolving lives, aging.
sentences.zh: 它是我们对自身不断变化、发展和老去的生活的一种衡量标准。

sentences.en: And I think also for the passage of time in a larger sense over the centuries to which we are connected.
sentences.zh: 我也认为，这代表着我们在与之相连的数个世纪里更广阔意义上的时间流逝。

sentences.en: And the building's resurrection preserves that connection.
sentences.zh: 而这座建筑的复活保留了这种联系。

sentences.en: It allows us to think we can go back.
sentences.zh: 它让我们觉得我们可以回到过去。

sentences.en: We haven't lost touch, essentially, with not just with the past, but with ourselves.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，我们不仅没有与过去失去联系，也没有与自我失去联系。

sentences.en: Just before I left the cathedral, I was speaking with a woman who showed us around.
sentences.zh: 就在我离开大教堂之前，我正和一位带我们参观的女士交谈。

sentences.en: And I asked her directly, are you Catholic?
sentences.zh: 我直接问她，你是天主教徒吗？

sentences.en: And she said, yes.
sentences.zh: 她说，是的。

sentences.en: So I said to her, what has it meant for you to be working on this project?
sentences.zh: 所以我对她说，参与这个项目对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: And she struggled for like a minute to find the words.
sentences.zh: 她挣扎了一分钟才找到合适的词。

sentences.en: And then she wept.
sentences.zh: 然后她哭了。

sentences.en: And I thought that said it all, really.
sentences.zh: 我心想，这真是一切尽在不言中。

sentences.en: That for her, this was also something that she would remember for the rest of her life.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，这也是她余生都会铭记的事情。

sentences.en: That she lived at this moment.
sentences.zh: 她经历了这个时刻。

sentences.en: For her, no doubt had religious meanings.
sentences.zh: 对她而言，这无疑具有宗教意义。

sentences.en: But I'd like to think is the power of architecture and can sustain us at a time when we are divided and we sometimes lose hope.
sentences.zh: 但我更愿意认为，这是建筑的力量，能够在我们分化、有时甚至失去希望的时代支撑我们。

sentences.en: Maybe that was the original idea for the people who built the cathedral nearly a thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是近一千年前建造大教堂的人们的初衷。

sentences.en: Oh, Michael, on that really beautiful note, thank you very, very much.
sentences.zh: 哦，迈克尔，伴随着如此美妙的感触，非常非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
